title: Choose crypz's new visual world
question: The current look (monochrome ink/bone, zero-radius squares, tiny mono everywhere) is being replaced. The roll assigned Pit Wall Debrief. Keep it, take the pick, or re-roll.

options.label: Pit Wall Debrief
options.lineage: motorsport pit-wall session review — sector times, deltas, personal bests
options.thesis: Every closed session gets read like a race debrief: sectors, deltas, personal bests, flagged risk.
options.viewport: Sidebar + top bar unchanged in structure; stat cards get a coloured sector-tab (violet = personal best, amber = high-leverage flag); the cumulative curve becomes a lap-trace bar strip colouring its best and worst sessions; edge-by-instrument reads like a sector-time sheet.
options.risk: Can tip into literal racing iconography (checkered flags, speedometers) if the motorsport reference is taken as decoration instead of a colour-and-pacing discipline.

raised.raise: Every live-updating figure (price, funding countdown, equity) arrives as a visible mechanical update — a brief digit-roll, never a silent re-render — borrowed as discipline, not as flap-board skin.

One reserved accent (violet) is spent only on the single most load-bearing flagged number per screen — the one metric that should change behaviour — kept scarce everywhere else so the new colour range doesn't turn noisy.

options.label: Training Log
options.lineage: athlete's performance journal — streaks, PRs, activity calendar
options.thesis: The dashboard reads like a training log: warm, encouraging, built around streaks and personal records instead of a ledger of losses.
options.viewport: Same sidebar/top-bar shell, warmed and rounded; stat cards softened with generous padding; a 30-day activity calendar and a profit-factor progress ring replace the stat-dense strip as the emotional centre; recent trades read as a short warm list, not a ledger.
options.risk: Most familiar of the set — reads like a modern fitness or habit app. Comfortable and legible, but the safest-feeling option and the one most likely to feel imported rather than this product's own voice.

options.label: Split-Flap Concourse
options.case: Fuses cleanly for live-updating rows (positions, order flow) but a crypto trader doesn't identify with a transit concourse, and an all-flap composition fights the dense multi-chart layout this product needs.
options.kept: Donated its mechanical-update discipline to the assigned direction.

options.label: Character Goods Catalog
options.case: No identification or clarity for a product about real trading losses — cute mascot ranking reads as a toy, not a performance tool.

options.label: Warm Consumer App
options.case: This is the generic-SaaS outcome you explicitly want to avoid — card stack on a tinted ground with one action colour, too shallow for a dense data-review tool.
options.kept: Nothing carried forward — named here so it's visibly ruled out, not silently avoided.

options.label: Centre-Rail Reference Setting
options.case: Beautiful precision but a trader doesn't identify with a critical edition manuscript, and twin-column prose doesn't fit a chart-and-table product.
options.kept: Donated its one-scarce-accent discipline to the assigned direction.

options.label: Mixtape J-Card
options.case: Charming but the audience mismatch is total — a mixtape has no relationship to reviewing derivatives trades.

options.label: Orienteering Map
options.lineage: ISOM orienteering map and course legend
options.case: An interesting fixed-colour-means-one-thing legend, but a trader doesn't identify with wilderness navigation, and the map-as-ground conflicts with a chart-and-table layout.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The clean modern analytics dashboard this category always ships: white ground, rounded cards, one blue accent.
canonCard.viewport: Standard sidebar, white stat cards with light shadows, a blue equity chart, a plain instrument table.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other trading/analytics SaaS — safe, but exactly the 'plain and generic' outcome you're trying to leave behind.
